title: ITSM incident queue: triage, SLA pause and resume, problem records, CAB gate
spec_author: Opus 5.5 (this build session), 2026-11-04; never edited after a result was read

host.alt: sqlite-mcp through the breadth facade (field reserved; not built)

sources.what: UCI incident management process enriched event log (ID 498, CC BY 4.0): weekday arrival shares, priority mix, pause (Awaiting) share, resolution-time quantiles and mined SLA thresholds (P3 91.68 h, P4 328.53 h)
sources.kind: observed data, parameters only (research/breadth-20261021/factory/params/uci-498-params.json); CSV deleted
inference: common ITSM practice, our own 3x3 table; not a claim about any product

fiction: All organisations, people, addresses, systems and incidents are fictional (*.example domains).

params.matrix: impact + urgency (1 high, 2 medium, 3 low): 2 -> P1, 3 -> P2, 4 -> P3, 5 or 6 -> P4

clauses.title: Triage
clauses.text: At each scheduled check, every incident whose Priority is empty or `UNTRIAGED` and whose Impact and Urgency are both readable (`1`, `2`, `3`, optionally followed by ` - High/Medium/Low`, or just `High`, `Medium`, `Low`) is triaged: Priority = P1 when Impact + Urgency is 2, P2 when 3, P3 when 4, P4 when 5 or 6 (1 = High, 2 = Medium, 3 = Low); SLA Due = Opened At (any written UTC offset) + the target hours for that priority in force on Opened At's UTC date (SLA Policy Log). Write Priority (e.g. `P3`) and SLA Due (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). An incident with an empty Priority whose Impact or Urgency cannot be read: post one line naming the trigger id and the Incident ID in #{sink} and write Priority `UNTRIAGED`; it is triaged at the first check after both are readable.

clauses.title: SLA pause and resume
clauses.text: On a changed tracker row (not at checks): when a triaged incident's Status is `Awaiting User` and Paused Since is empty, write Paused Since = its Status Changed At. When its Status is anything else and Paused Since is filled, move SLA Due later by (Status Changed At - Paused Since) and clear Paused Since. A change that repeats what the tracker already shows changes nothing.

clauses.title: Breach
clauses.text: At each scheduled check, every triaged incident whose Status is not `Resolved` or `Closed`, whose Paused Since is empty, whose SLA Due is at or before the check and whose Breached At is empty: post `BREACHED <Incident ID> <Priority>` in #{escalation} and write the check time in Breached At.

clauses.title: Problem records
clauses.text: At each scheduled check, after triage: when {problem_min} or more incidents on the same CI (exact name) were opened in the {problem_window_hours} hours before the check and no incident on that CI has a Problem Ref, create one Jira issue in project PRB (issue type Problem) with the summary `Problem: <CI>` and write `PRB:<CI>` in Problem Ref of each of those incidents. Every later incident on a CI that already has a Problem Ref gets the same Problem Ref at the first check that sees it (no new issue).

clauses.title: CAB decisions
clauses.text: An email from exactly the CAB Chair (Config) that approves or rejects a change (`approve`/`approved` or `reject`/`rejected` and the exact Change ID) whose CAB Status is empty: on approval, if the change's CI has a triaged P1 incident whose Status is not `Resolved` or `Closed`, write CAB Status `On Hold` and Decided At (the email's trigger time) and post `CHANGE <Change ID> ON HOLD` in #{changes}; otherwise write CAB Status `Approved` and Decided At and post `CHANGE <Change ID> APPROVED`. On rejection write `Rejected` and Decided At and post `CHANGE <Change ID> REJECTED`. A decision from any other address: post one line naming the trigger id and the Change ID in #{sink} and change nothing. A decision for a change already decided, or an unknown Change ID: nothing.

clauses.title: Policy editions
clauses.text: The SLA Policy Log holds one row per edition and parameter (`P1 target hours` ... `P4 target hours`); for a parameter, the row in force on a date is the one with the latest Effective date not after it. An email from exactly the Service Owner (Config) with the lines `Parameter: <name>`, `New value: <hours>` and `Effective: <YYYY-MM-DD>` adds one Policy Log row: Edition = the highest edition + 1, the Parameter, the Value (digits only), the Effective date, Approved by = the owner's address. Incidents opened before that date keep their SLA Due. A value outside {value_range_lo}-{value_range_hi} hours: post one line naming the trigger id in #{sink} and add nothing. The same request from anyone else: nothing.

clauses.title: Month-end
clauses.text: The {month_end_check} UTC check on the last working day of a month (Holidays sheet) also posts `MONTH-END <YYYY-MM> breached=<n> open=<m>` in #{reports}, after that check's other work: n = incidents whose Breached At is in that month (UTC); m = triaged incidents whose Status is not `Resolved` or `Closed`.

clauses.title: Quiet events
clauses.text: A new incident or change row needs nothing at once: the next check triages incidents, and changes wait for a CAB email. Changed rows other than the pause and resume of Q2 (reassignment, description edits, resolution) need nothing.

triggers.check: 09:00, 11:00, 14:00, 17:00 UTC on working days (Holidays sheet, England)
triggers.updated: updated_row on Incidents (status, assignment or description changes)
triggers.email: new_email to the automation inbox (CAB decisions, policy amendments, noise)

traps.what: three incidents on one CI inside an hour; incidents on that CI older than the window do not count
the same status change or CAB email delivered twice
an incident logged without Impact or Urgency, completed later
a change approved while its CI has an open P1 incident goes On Hold
CI db-prod-01 vs db-prod-011; a look-alike CAB chair address
an older 120-hour P3 row; the new P3 target applies by Opened At, not by check time
Opened At written with a UTC offset; Impact as `2 - Medium`, `Medium` or `2`

golden.rule: mined from UCI 498 (made_sla vs resolution hours)

headline.metric: clean stream (4 weeks, zero hard violations, every week passing)
